note: No caption is printed: these are the five resonating structures of aniline, drawn as a displayed row with no 'Figure 9.x' line, so `caption` is left empty rather than invented. All five rings are DRAWN as hexagons with no typed formula; only printed text is listed, left to right -- each structure's nitrogen label (and, for structures II, III and IV, the negative charge printed on the ring carbon that bears it) -- followed by the row of Roman numerals printed beneath (rows 467-500, inside the box). The flat list cannot show which charge sits on which ring carbon, nor that numeral I names the first structure and V the fifth; that structure is lost. Charge signs are printed as a '+' set above the NH2 of structures II, III and IV, written here as a leading '+'. Structure I prints a lone pair as two dots to the LEFT of its N and structure V prints one as two dots ABOVE its N; dots cannot be placed in a flat text label. The four linking double-headed resonance arrows and the curved pink electron-shift arrows on every structure carry no text and cannot be represented. Over-included by the crop and excluded: the preceding paragraph ('pKb value of aniline is quite high. ... aniline is a resonance hybrid of the following five structures.', its first line clipped at the top edge) and the following lines ('On the other hand, anilinium ion obtained by accepting a proton can have only two resonating structures (kekule).', cut by the bottom edge).
